answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so influence depends on paths supported by attestations, not on claimed identities. When a sybil cluster connects to honest participants through few edges, its sparse external cut yields low conductance; under volume-normalized voting, this bottleneck bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight despite many internal nodes. A thread of evidence must cross the cut: a willow-thin bridge cannot carry unlimited influence, even at dawn.
